# Retired repositories and websites

The public recovery releases were intentionally deleted on September 30, 2026.
DSPIRA and the lab website no longer download their archives or publish the
archive-dependent institute, CRA, and transient website copies.

## Current website ownership

- DSPIRA publishes current lessons, teaching resources, and downloads from active repositories.
- The historical experiment catalog and lab images remain under `/dspira/history/`.
  Their files are stored in this repository and do not depend on release assets.
- The lab site maintains `/dspira-lessons/` compatibility paths for current lessons
  and the `/gr-dspira/` redirect to the current software guide.
- The lab workflow runs hourly to refresh current lesson redirects.
- The former `/dspira/history/sites/`, `/dspira-archive/`, `/cra/`, and
  `/gr-transient/` publications are retired. Do not link current pages to them.

Original source records, author credits, and licenses stay with retained files.
The current repository map identifies maintained projects and replacement links.

## Software repository name swap

On September 25, the original `gr-dspira` repository became the active
`dspira-software` repository. Its GitHub repository ID is `139190089`.
Its default branch includes the current software and both projects' Git histories.
Its original star, fork, and contributor history remain attached to that repository.

The former `dspira-software` repository took the name `gr-dspira` with repository
ID `1386771762`. Both software issues moved to the active repository and retained
their numbers. Use repository IDs when distinguishing the historical projects.

## Preservation record

Before retirement, five recovery packages captured 573 default-branch files,
Git refs, branches, tags, public GitHub records, and restoration instructions.
The institute package also included its wiki and all 35 historical LFS objects.
The bundles were restored into fresh repositories, and refs, source files,
large-file contents, and ZIP integrity were verified.

Those checks describe the offline recovery copies. The deleted releases are no
longer public download destinations or website build dependencies.
Git history retains the earlier manifests and publication records.
